result.summary: Moves process-wide block template statistics from BlockAssembler into per-instance fields, recording them in BlockTemplateManager under cs_main. The getmininginfo RPC is updated to read currentblockweight and currentblocktx from BlockTemplateManager rather than process-wide statics.
result.problem: getmininginfo reads global static variables that lack thread-safety annotations and are overwritten by any call to BlockAssembler::CreateNewBlock(). Background operations like mempool fee estimation build templates with BlockAssembler, causing getmininginfo to report fee estimation templates instead of actual mining templates, while also hindering multi-node context isolation.
evidence: PR description: "getmininginfo reports currentblockweight and currentblocktx from two process-wide statics, BlockAssembler::m_last_block_weight and m_last_block_num_txs, which every BlockAssembler::CreateNewBlock() call overwrites... the mempool fee estimator builds its own templates with BlockAssembler, so getmininginfo can report the fee estimator's template instead of the last mining template."

Commit e47e7acca3: "Behavior change: only templates built through BlockTemplateManager (getblocktemplate, the generate RPCs and the mining interface) update these fields. Templates that the mempool fee estimator builds with BlockAssembler directly no longer do..."
Issue #33758: completes the 'Remove remaining global states' item in the BlockTemplateManager tracking issue.
result.scope_notes: Stacked on PR #36356; the diff includes commits from #36356 that move getblocktemplate caching into BlockTemplateManager.
result.card: Moves process-wide block statistics from BlockAssembler into instance variables and stores mining stats in BlockTemplateManager under cs_main. Currently, getmininginfo reads unannotated global statics that are overwritten by any template build across the process, including non-mining templates generated by the mempool fee estimator. With this change, getmininginfo reports metrics solely from templates built for mining, and template state is cleanly scoped to each node context. Based on PR #36356.

risk.why: Holding cs_main across template creation or mishandling template cache state could introduce locking contention or report inaccurate mining statistics in RPC responses.
